name: Multiple Paragangliomas Associated with Polycythemia

criteria.description: Presence of two or more paragangliomas confirmed by imaging or histopathology
Documented elevated hemoglobin and hematocrit levels consistent with polycythemia
Elevated serum erythropoietin levels or evidence of erythropoietin secretion by tumor
Identification of pathogenic mutations in genes associated with paragangliomas and polycythemia (e.g., HIF2A/EPAS1)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of multiple paragangliomas plus documented polycythemia
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but is not mandatory.

searchTerms: multiple paraganglioma tumors seen on scans

pathognomonic.symptomName: Secondary polycythemia with elevated hemoglobin and hematocrit
searchTerms: high red blood cell count with increased hemoglobin
high blood pressure from hormone secretion

common.symptomName: Headache related to tumor mass effect or hypertension
searchTerms: headache from tumor pressure or high blood pressure
painful head due to mass effect or hypertension

occasional.symptomName: Abdominal or neck mass palpable on physical exam
searchTerms: palpable mass in abdomen or neck
abdominal or neck swelling felt by doctor

occasional.symptomName: Visual disturbances due to polycythemia-related hyperviscosity
searchTerms: eye symptoms caused by blood thickening

rare.symptomName: Transient ischemic attacks or stroke due to hyperviscosity
searchTerms: transient ischemic attacks caused by hyperviscosity
stroke-like episodes due to blood viscosity
burning pain and redness in extremities
limb pain with redness related to polycythemia
nerve damage causing facial muscle weakness

imaging: MRI or CT showing multiple paragangliomas in typical locations (head, neck, abdomen)
Functional imaging (e.g., 123I-MIBG scintigraphy, PET scan) demonstrating tumor activity
other: Evidence of erythropoietin secretion by tumor tissue

distinguishingFeatures: Primary bone marrow disorder with JAK2 mutation
Single tumor rather than multiple lesions

redFlags: Rapidly increasing hemoglobin and hematocrit levels
Neurological deficits suggestive of ischemic events
